target.title: fix(codex): reject hex/exponent computer wait duration strings
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Codex computer `wait` / `hold_key` outer watchdog deadlines used JavaScript `Number(...)` on free-form `duration` values. Hex strings such as `"0x10"` were accepted (`Number("0x10") === 16`) and silently inflated the deadline, while the downstream computer tool already rejects hex via `readFiniteNumberParam` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Codex contract (sibling `../codex` inspected):** dynamic-tool arguments are `serde_json::Value` with no field-level `duration` guard — `DynamicToolHandler` parses JSON and forwards the value unchanged (`codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:136`, checkout `bdd282f3bbd55df3a869a5438519cd948c134d4d`). OpenClaw pins `@openai/codex@0.144.4`.

**Canonical downstream grammar (OpenClaw computer tool):**
- Schema: `optionalFiniteNumberSchema` in `src/agents/tools/computer-tool.ts:161`
- Runtime: `readFiniteNumberParam` → `readNumberParam({ strict: true })` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber` (`src/agents/tools/common.ts:228`, `computer-tool.ts:856`)

That parser **rejects hex** (`"0x10"`) and **accepts** decimal / scientific / fractional strings (`"100"`, `"1e2"`, `"100.5"`, `"0.5"`) plus finite numbers.

This PR makes the Codex outer watchdog use the **same** `parseStrictFiniteNumber` path so hex inflation is fixed without underbudgeting fractional/scientific strings that computer-tool still honors.

Collision: overlaps [#107623](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107623); this head is the rebased, contract-aligned form.

## User Impact

| Duration input | Before (`Number()`) | After (computer-tool grammar) |
|---|---|---|
| `"0x10"` | +16s inflation | baseline (rejected) |
| `"1e2"` / `"100.5"` / `"0.5"` | coerced | honored (aligned) |
| `0.5` (number) | honored | honored |

## Evidence

Exact head: `d85b72dabe57770b68e901f974a448729cf05581`

### Call path

```
Codex app-server request
  → run-attempt-server-requests.ts:191  resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs({ call, config })
    → dynamic-tool-execution.ts          readComputerToolTimeoutMs / readComputerDurationMs
      → parseStrictFiniteNumber(value)   ← same grammar as computer-tool
    → handleDynamicToolCallWithTimeout({ timeoutMs })
```

### Focused Vitest

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Codex computer `wait`/`hold_key` outer watchdog no longer inflates on hex `duration` (`"0x10"`), while still honoring scientific/fractional durations that computer-tool accepts.
- Real environment tested: Windows 10 + Node v24.17.0 + local checkout at `d85b72dabe57770b68e901f974a448729cf05581`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  ```bash
  node --import tsx .tmp/proof-computer-duration-watchdog.mts
  ```
  Local-only harness (not committed): exercises `parseStrictFiniteNumber` plus the production `readComputerToolTimeoutMs` budget formula used by `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` at `run-attempt-server-requests.ts:191`.
- Evidence after fix:
  ```text
  === Codex computer duration watchdog proof (local only) ===
  node=v24.17.0
  head=d85b72dabe57770b68e901f974a448729cf05581
  grammar=parseStrictFiniteNumber (@openclaw/normalization-core)
  budget=readComputerToolTimeoutMs formula from dynamic-tool-execution.ts
  caller=run-attempt-server-requests.ts:191 → resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs

  Shared grammar:
  {"100":100,"0x10":null,"1e2":100,"0.5":0.5}

  BEFORE (Number coercion inflates hex):
  {"duration":"0x10","Number_value":16,"inflated_timeoutMs":136000}

  AFTER fix (strict grammar + computer budget):
  {"hex_0x10_wait":{"timeoutMs":120000},"scientific_1e2_hold_key":{"timeoutMs":250000},"fraction_0_5_wait":{"timeoutMs":120500},"decimal_100_wait":{"timeoutMs":220000},"numeric_0_5_wait":{"timeoutMs":120500}}

    ok: hex grammar rejected
    ok: hex timeout baseline 120000 (not 136000)
    ok: scientific 1e2 → 250000
    ok: fraction 0.5 → 120500
    ok: decimal 100 → 220000
    ok: numeric 0.5 → 120500

  === Summary ===
  ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 6 passed, 0 failed
  ```
- Observed result after fix: Hex `"0x10"` stays at the 120000ms baseline (broken `Number()` path would be 136000). Scientific `"1e2"` and fractional `"0.5"` keep honored outer budgets (250000 / 120500).
- What was not tested: Live Codex app-server ↔ node computer round-trip with a real computer node / API key.

## Current review state

- Next action: ClawSweeper re-review after local runtime proof was pasted (proof harness kept local-only; not pushed).
- Waiting on: `proof: sufficient` label routing + maintainer look.
- Addressed: prior P1 asking for after-fix evidence of rejected hex vs accepted fractional/scientific duration budgets on the resolve path used by the app-server dynamic-tool handler.
